verdicts.title: Stop hiding zoom tools mid-run: the changed tool list breaks the prefix cache for the final submit request
verdicts.reason: The code matches. sever/image_agent.py:256-265 prepare_zoom returns None once zoom_count>=8 or requests_started>=7; :278-289 holds the in-tool decline; :302 zoom_regions accepts max_length=8, so one call can use all 8 crops; sever/image_conflicts.py:461-466 does the same. In pydantic_ai/models/__init__.py:264-265 tool_defs = [*function_tools, *output_tools], so the zoom tools are listed BEFORE submit_reading, and removing them changes the prompt at the tools block, before the submit schema and every image. Three things are still unverified. (a) That the deployed Qwen3.8 chat template renders tools in the first system turn ahead of the images; this is true for Qwen2.5/3 templates, but the GGUF template was not checked. (b) How often this happens. (c) The 'whole slot clears' consequence, which applies only if the model is hybrid, and that is unconfirmed. The fingerprint/prompt-hash change, which forces a new batch, is not mentioned.

verdicts.title: Emit crop rectangles as integer [x1,y1,x2,y2] in 0-1000 instead of keyed floats in [0,1]
verdicts.reason: The code matches: sever/image_agent.py:36 float Coordinate in [0,1], :55-60 CropRegion keyed floats, :75-76 instruction text, :180-189 zoom scaling, :302 up to 8 regions; image_conflicts.py:145-150 _FrameCropRegion. The token arithmetic is plausible, since Qwen tokenizers split digits one per token. The main assumption is unmeasured: that zoom arguments are 30-40% of the 222 output tokens per call. Submit_reading answers with evidence_text and raw_value (image_reader.py:161-167) probably dominate. The 'float re-serialisation' cache argument is speculative: pydantic-ai sends the raw argument string back, and any re-render by the server's template would differ in spacing too, not only in floats. The 0-1000 convention for Qwen3.8 is unverified.

verdicts.title: Send the context, orientation and triage images at the server's token window, not 1024 px that the server then bilinear-upscales
verdicts.reason: sever/image_agent.py:140-146 runs LANCZOS thumbnail to 1024 then JPEG q95. :170-173 prep records resize 'none' and native_source_detail for crops. :77-78 promises crops 'without magnification'. image_detail.py:84-90 shrinks the orientation images to 1024 px, and image_triage.py:133-134 sends the single context JPEG. b7822 clip.cpp:1158-1171 (QWEN3VL) shows the min-1024-token warning; :2833-2843 calc_size_preserved_ratio(patch_size*2, min, max) followed by RESIZE_ALGO_BILINEAR; :2357-2361 upscales below min_pixels. A 2160x3840 frame becomes 576x1024 = 589,824 px, below the 1024-token minimum, so the server upscales it. This holds only if the deployed v0.6.0 keeps the same preprocessing and patch size; the exact pixel window must be read from the startup log. Uplifting small crops on the client with LANCZOS is still magnification, so the instruction text must change to match.

verdicts.title: A/B the already-installed Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE) against the dense 27B on the current pipeline: the user decides
verdicts.reason: deploy/README.md:166 records the user's choice of the dense 27B. :236-245 shows the old trial was OCR-guided, with accepted-field counters ('не независимо измеренная точность'). :254 says the 35B model is kept. The speed estimate is optimistic against the only measurement on hand: that trial gave 156.8 vs 231.2 s, about 32% less time, against the claimed -45 to -60%. The 150-200 tok/s decode is an assumption. At Q6 the 35B weights are about 28-29 GB, which leaves almost no room for --parallel or a larger ctx on 32 GB.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Expect somewhere between the old trial's -32% and the -45 to -60% estimate. Keep it an opt-in experiment that needs the user's consent and a full re-score on 44 labels.

verdicts.title: Raise --ubatch-size to 1024-2048: prefill becomes the bottleneck once decode is batched
verdicts.reason: deploy/sever-model.service:12 sets no -b/-ub. b7822 common.h:322-323 defaults to n_batch 2048 / n_ubatch 512. Prefill is 273 of 1004 model seconds, which is 27% (analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:22-23). The 10-25% gain is not measured, and prompt_ms includes vision-encoder time, which ubatch does not speed up. llama-bench -p measures text-only prefill and will overstate the gain for image-heavy prompts.

verdicts.title: Cap output tokens per call kind at about 2x the observed maximum instead of 8192 for agent and joint-review calls
verdicts.reason: deploy/local-provider.env.example:7 sets HARNESS_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8192, and deploy/README.md:167 says the output limit is 8192. sever/cli.py:27 and sever/api.py:157 default to '2200'. image_agent.py:328 and image_conflicts.py:528 pass max_tokens. image_orientation.py:28 caps at 128 and image_triage.py:30 at 96. The effect only touches tail latency and is unknown until the trace is read. Long address raw_value (max_length 1200, image_reader.py:161) across 6 fields can legitimately run to several thousand tokens, so the floor must come from data.

verdicts.title: If the model is hybrid, shrink the static prefix (instructions plus about 14.8k-char schema): it is re-prefilled on every run
verdicts.reason: The b7822 code matches: server-context.cpp:1007-1008 mtmd skips the prompt cache, :2290-2298 checkpoints are disabled with mtmd, :2434-2441 a failed truncate clears the memory. image_reader.py:163/:211 'Omit' fields exist. The premise is unresolved, and the measurements point both ways. Idle VRAM of 26,180 MiB suggests a small KV, which fits a hybrid model. Yet 68% of input tokens came from the cache, and only 639,726 tokens were prefilled over 188 calls, about 3.4k per call. Every crop costs at least 1024 tokens, and orientation sends 4 images. If about 70 runs each re-prefilled a 7-8k prefix, the new-token total would probably exceed that figure. So cross-run reuse may already work. The finding is correctly conditional.

verdicts.title: Read a leaf's first two frames concurrently to shorten the critical path
verdicts.reason: The code shows sequential reads: native_pipeline.py:862 awaits read inside the per-frame loop, and :1066-1090 runs concurrency only across leaves. zoom_image_reader.py:41-61 reuses the leaf's orientation. comparison.md gives page-0015 34 calls and 301.33 s. Leaves 0007-0010 stop after 3 calls (orientation, triage and 1 read?), so starting two reads at once would add a wasted second read on leaves that one triage result could settle. The saturation/redundancy check (native_pipeline.py:855-859) and the no-progress counter depend on order. The gain is not quantified from data, and the effort is L.

verdicts.title: Do not spend time on speculative decoding, --cache-reuse, --cache-ram, lower --image-min-tokens or f16 KV
verdicts.reason: b7822 server-context.cpp:712-736: with multimodal, cache_reuse is disabled, a speculative draft makes load return false, and memory that cannot shift also disables cache_reuse. :1007-1008 mtmd skips the RAM prompt cache. clip.cpp:1166-1171 prints the Qwen-VL grounding warning. common/arg.cpp in b7822 has --reasoning-format/--reasoning-budget and no --no-reasoning-preserve, which confirms the deployed binary (v0.6.0, deploy/README.md:254) is newer. The report rightly says to re-check every point on that binary.

missing: The deployed llama.cpp is a 'v0.6.0' tag archive (deploy/README.md:254), not the local b7822 checkout. Every finding that relies on b7822 behaviour (KV split, slot selection, mtmd cache/checkpoint rules, Qwen-VL resize) needs to be re-verified on the server binary first, and only findings 2 and 10 say so.

Crop prefill floor: --image-min-tokens 1024 applies to every zoom crop, so each small caption crop costs at least about 1024 prefill tokens after server upscaling. 8 crops per frame read means at least about 8k new tokens per run. The report never puts a number on crop count or crop token cost as a prefill lever, for example fewer or merged crops, or one composite image per zoom_regions call.

About half of the measured 11.8% GPU idle is the first 14 samples (about 70 s) of pre-model video analysis (gpu-phase1-speed.csv). Leaf concurrency within one video cannot hide it; overlapping the analysis of video k+1 with the reading of video k can.

Calls per sheet remain the dominant lever: page-0015 (34 calls, 301 s) and the two TTN other-side leaves (19-22 calls) set the critical path. No serving-side finding addresses the stop rules for 'requires_other_document_side'.

Accuracy gating: findings 1 and 7 propose re-scoring only the 22 labels of video 5. 44 labelled fields over 4 videos exist, and with 22 labels the 95% interval spans about 50-87% (ab README), so a speed change cannot be shown accuracy-neutral on video 5 alone.

Request timeout and fairness under --parallel: HARNESS_MODEL_TIMEOUT=600 and deferred pinned tasks are not analysed, and neither is the effect of N=4 on per-request latency during long prefill of a joint review.
The implementation fingerprint and prompt hash change (deploy/README.md:455-460) affects findings 3, 4, 5 and 9 and forces a new batch. The report flags this for only some of them.

verdicts.title: Enable MTP self-speculative decoding on the existing llama.cpp v0.6.0 + Qwen3.8-27B Q6
verdicts.reason: Repo: deploy/sever-model.service:12 has no --spec-type and runs --parallel 1, q8_0 KV; deploy/README.md:259 says v0.6.0; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md says 688 s generation at 61 tok/s = 69% of model time, 5.34 s/request, 188 requests. Web: github.com/sudoingX/qwen38-mtp has the RTX 5090 Q6_K row 61.9 -> 130.0 at n-max 2, acceptance 0.52-0.95, +110%, and the --parallel 1 rule. PR #22673 is 'llama + spec: MTP Support', merged around 2026-05-16, uses --spec-type draft-mtp and --spec-draft-n-max, and has a 5090 row 63.72 -> 105.47 (acc 0.797). The HF Qwen3.8-27B card says MTP is 'trained with multiple steps'. Issue #27428 shows 766 -> 742 (3%) for a single-GPU 4090 run, though it was Q3_K_XL and the report's 'Laptop' detail is not stated. ROCmFPX #67 gives 7.533/0.611 s on stock b10400. The newreleases v0.4.1 page has the #28715 'Fixed speculative decoding after image input' line. The reddit snapshot reports image-turn acceptance 0.62 at 104.68 tok/s. The v0.6.0 release exists (05 Oct) and mentions MTP speculative decoding. Arithmetic checks out: 3.66 s decode of 5.34 s, and about 3.46-4.01 s per call after the speedup. Recomputing the video wall (1,134 - 1,004 + 188 x 3.4-4.0 s) gives about 770-880 s, slightly above the reported 750-850 s.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Numbers and sources check out. Two corrections. First, the derived phase1 video-5 wall is about 770-880 s, not 750-850 s. Second, every cited MTP gain comes from long text generations (128K-ctx benchmarks, 2,000-token runs), while our calls emit about 222-token JSON tool calls after large image prefixes, so the realized gain may sit at the low end. The v0.6.0 notes also add 'probabilistic sampling for simple draft and MTP', so check that the temperature-0 path stays greedy-verified. Whether the deployed UD-Q6_K_M GGUF contains MTP tensors is still unverified.

verdicts.title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE) gives the largest raw per-call speedup but needs a labelled accuracy A/B
verdicts.reason: The HF Qwen3.6-35B-A3B card exists and is Apache-2.0, April 2026: OmniDocBench1.5 89.9, CC-OCR 81.9, MMMU 81.7, 40 layers, 256 experts (8 routed + 1 shared), 2 KV heads. jarvislabs (RTX PRO 6000, Q8_0): 27B 45.76 -> 79.37 with MTP, 35B-A3B 193.36 -> 225.48 (1.17x). hardware-corner 5090 Q4_K_XL: 2931.32/61.38 vs 6630.42/234.30. atomic.chat (b10988): 3,830/74.2 vs Nemotron 12,047/334.3. BenchLM CC-OCR: 81.2 vs 81.9. Roboflow: 64.8% vs 69.5%. The decode ratio of about 3.8-4.2x is supported. The prefill upper bound of 3.1x comes from Nemotron, a different model; the only Qwen MoE-vs-dense pair gives 2.26x. The VRAM risk is overstated: deploy/README.md:260 shows Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6 was already deployed on this very 5090 for the historical trial, so Q6 does fit with mmproj.

The Q6 build is already proven to fit the server (deploy/README.md:260), so dropping to Q5 for VRAM reasons is unnecessary. Quality evidence is limited to generic benchmarks, with no Cyrillic data.

verdicts.title: Concurrency 2-4 on llama.cpp: modest gain, poor fit with MTP, wall capped by slowest leaf
verdicts.reason: sever/cli.py:29-30 matches the quoted leaf_concurrency env var. comparison.md:45 shows page-0015 at 301.33 s, and the wall is 1,134.49 s. computingforgeeks ?p=171658 has 5090 rows llama.cpp 77.8 single / 369 at 32 and vLLM 85.7 / 936, but the engines ran different quants (llama.cpp UD-Q4_K_M, vLLM RedHatAI INT4 W4A16). sudoingX's README says a parallel-2 baseline 'reads ~20% low' and the advantage is 'gone by 4 concurrent streams'. Jan PR #9186 shows RS 598.5 -> 2394.0 MiB from 1 to 4 slots ('about 600 MiB each') with MTP, at UD-Q2_K_XL and 8k ctx. Particula describes the slot-reassignment collapse with 15 x 149.626 MiB checkpoints discarded (issue #22746). The 1.3-2.0x throughput figures are the report's own estimates with no direct measurement, as it admits. id_slot is not used anywhere in sever/, so pinning needs a code change.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Sources are accurate. The 369-vs-936 comparison mixes quantizations (GGUF Q4_K_M vs GPTQ W4A16), so it overstates llama.cpp's weakness somewhat. The critical-path bound only bites at 4 slots (1,134/4 = 284 s < 301 s); at 2 slots it does not. Pinning workers to slots with id_slot needs new code in the harness.

verdicts.title: vLLM 0.31 + nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (+MTP) is the throughput option for 4+ concurrent streams
verdicts.reason: The nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 card exists: Apache-2.0, dated 09/08/2026, MLP + lm_head NVFP4 and attention/linear-attention FP8, MMMU-Pro 75.14->74.86, IFBench 80.07->78.93, qwen3_coder parser, no OCR eval. The Friendli gittensor card (vLLM 0.27.1, 2026-08-14, 5090) shows 80.6 / 137 / 267 tok/s, TTFT 134 ms at about 1,967 tokens and 8.52 s at about 62k, and a BF16 vision tower. The vLLM recipe calls Mamba prefix caching 'experimental in align mode' and says FP8 needs a 40 GB GPU. The Twu31 card reports 0% hits on a 1449-token prompt with the default state, 72% with bf16 state + block-aligned prompts, and 784-token blocks, but on vLLM 0.24.0 and in prose, not table rows. The vLLM docs include image hashes in the extra hashes. Misattribution: the '413 vs 261 at 4 concurrent' MTP figures and the 85.7 single-stream top of the range come from computingforgeeks ?p=171658, which used RedHatAI INT4 W4A16, not NVFP4. computingforgeeks tensorrt-llm-vs-vllm (the NVIDIA NVFP4 run) gives 65.6/68.5 single stream and 1,195 at 32 streams. The 718 s was the whole first start, mostly FlashInfer, not FlashInfer alone. vLLM #40807/#40831 were not verified.
verdicts.corrected_claim: For the NVIDIA NVFP4 checkpoint on vLLM 0.31, single-stream speed is 65.6-68.5 tok/s, not up to 85.7. The 413-vs-261 MTP gain at 4 streams was measured on a different INT4 W4A16 checkpoint. The hybrid prefix-cache numbers come from vLLM 0.24. The 718 s is the total first-start time.

verdicts.title: Do not switch to NVFP4 GGUF in llama.cpp for this OCR task without an A/B
verdicts.reason: The reddit snapshot 1syxckc shows Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 on a 5090: b8966 vs b8967 gives pp2048@d8192 3117.80 -> 5005.44 and tg512@d8192 71.65 -> 71.61. atomic.chat shows NVFP4-MTP at 5,100/79.4 vs AD-Q4_K_M at 3,830/74.2. Reddit 1u1r8yy has Tormeister's line 'NVFP4 and AWQ variants having much higher KLD than Q6_K quants' (Qwen3.6-27b). InsiderLLM confirms the conversion that dropped MTP (0% acceptance) and quality 'unsettled', and places native Blackwell NVFP4 at b8967. sudoingX has 62.7 -> 108.7 (n=3). Refuted sub-claim: neither the cited InsiderLLM page nor the reddit thread contains the 'NVFP4 perplexity 7.2 vs 6.6 for Q8_K_XL' comparison, and no source is given for it. The 'about 2x prefill' compares a llama-bench text number with our measured multimodal agent-workload 2,340 tok/s. The like-for-like llama-bench pair (Q4_K_M 3,830 vs NVFP4 5,100) is only 1.33x.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Drop the perplexity 7.2-vs-6.6 claim, which has no source. The like-for-like prefill gain over K-quants is about 1.3x, not 2x. Decode is about 72-79 tok/s. The recommendation to keep Q6 + MTP stands.

verdicts.title: KV cache: drop q8_0 to f16 (or shrink ctx); cheap for this hybrid model, not a speed lever
verdicts.reason: The HF Qwen3.8-27B card gives 64 layers in 16 blocks of 3 Gated DeltaNet + 1 Gated Attention, with 4 KV heads x 256 dim. That makes 16 x 4 x 256 x 2 (K+V) x 2 bytes = 64 KiB/token f16, which is 4 GiB at 65,536. q8_0 at 8.5 bits is about 2.1 GiB, so the delta is about 1.9 GiB. Jan PR #9186 measured 512 MiB KV at 8192 ctx, consistent with that. localbench gives 0.024 for Qwen 3.6 27B dense, but the sentence does not name the cache type explicitly. HN 48545335 has the lloyd-christmas quote 'quantizing k leads to broken json on tool calls'. The repo's 26,180-26,683 MiB matches. The claimed speed impact of 'within about 5%' has no source.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The memory math and sources are correct. The KL figure of 0.024 is only implied to be q8_0, and the speed-neutral claim is unsourced. With MTP (about 2 GB) plus f16 KV (+1.9 GB), usage reaches about 30.6 of 32.6 GB, so shrink ctx or keep q8_0 if MTP is enabled.

verdicts.title: Verify hybrid-model prompt-cache checkpoints are not forcing re-prefill
verdicts.reason: deploy/sever-model.service:12 has --chat-template-kwargs enable_thinking false and --no-reasoning-preserve. The README's 68% cache figure gives 639,726/188 = 3,403 new tokens per call, and a full re-prefill of 10,596 tokens at 2,340 tok/s is about 4.5 s. The llama.cpp server README has -ctxcp default 32, -cms default 8192 (0 = no minimum), -cram default 8192, and --reasoning-preserve default enabled. Particula describes -cms as an eviction floor, the 'forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data' message at verbosity 4, '-rea off' still churning context, and stripped empty think blocks changing the prefix. Since --no-reasoning-preserve strips reasoning from all but the last assistant message, it is a direct suspect for that churn in multi-turn agent loops.

verdicts.title: Candidate: Qwen3.8-27B EXL3 8.0bpw on ExLlamaV3 1.4.2
verdicts.reason: The HF card confirms every quoted number and the over-32 GB peak (34,634 MiB at 212,992 ctx). A 5090 fit at 8.0bpw is unlikely even at short ctx, since the weights alone are 27.35 GiB.

missing: The biggest accuracy loss is segmentation: 8/20 target intervals are missed in video.py ORB/RANSAC grouping. No engine or model change addresses it, and none of the findings improve precision; they all aim at speed-neutral or speed-positive swaps.
Call count per sheet is the larger lever. The 4 hard leaves take 72% of calls, and the 'requires_other_document_side' leaves burn 19-34 calls. Engine findings only cut per-call time.

Output-token reduction is missing: about 222 tokens per call, with decode at 69%. Shorter tool-call JSON, dropping verbose fields from submit_reading, or a terser schema is a zero-risk decode lever that also compounds with MTP.

Image token budget is unexamined: --image-min-tokens 1024 / --image-max-tokens 4096 and 1024 px context images. Measuring prompt_n per image and lowering the minimum for orientation/triage calls could cut prefill. The report also does not check whether the measured 2,340 tok/s 'prefill' excludes mmproj vision-encoder time, so comparisons with text llama-bench pp numbers are not like-for-like.

Every cited MTP speedup comes from long text generations. The short-output (about 222-token) regime with a large image prefix is unmeasured, and the first tokens after prefill are not drafted, so the gain could be lower.

Interaction of MTP with grammar-constrained or tool-call output (pydantic-ai NativeOutput/ToolOutput via json_schema grammar) in llama.cpp is unverified. So is the v0.6.0 change 'probabilistic sampling for simple draft and MTP' at temperature 0.

Determinism and business-rule impact: stored answers are never replayed, and the two-frame agreement rule makes any run-to-run numeric non-determinism (MTP batched verify, multi-slot batching, NVFP4) directly change confirmed/conflict outcomes. A repeated-run stability test (same frames, N runs) should precede any engine change.

--parallel N with --ctx-size 65536 may split the context per slot when the KV cache is not unified, shrinking each slot to 32k or 16k. Check the maximum per-call prompt (joint review up to 4 frames) first.

No OCR-specialised open-weight models (e.g. PaddleOCR-VL, dots.ocr, olmOCR-class) were evaluated as cheap first-pass readers or triage. With only 44 provisional labels (95% CI about 50-87%), no accuracy A/B can show parity; the label set needs to grow before any model swap.
No Russian or Cyrillic document-reading evidence exists for any candidate. The glyph errors seen in-house (РИТЕЙЛ->РИТЕИЛ, Кашириных->Каширных, соор.->корп.) need a targeted glyph-level test set.

verdicts.title: Let two independent single-frame 'other_document_side' claims end the leaf at view 2 without the joint review
verdicts.reason: The code matches the claim. sever/image_reader.py:159-167: ImageField has only a free-text `reason`, with no cause enum. native_pipeline.py:821-823 requires a leaf_visibility_assessments entry with source_reading_count == len(readings). Those entries are created only at :672-680 from a joint review, with image_conflicts.py:330-336 needs_other_side. complete_page_visible is already reading-level (image_reader.py:216, :429). comparison.json phase1 confirms joint calls 5/5/7/4/6/6 = 33 of 39, field_agent 15/12/6/7/11/26, views 2/2/2/2/2/5, and confirmed fields 1/1/0/2/0/2 in both runs. verdicts.title: After a non-terminal field review, allow one more view instead of three, and count progress only on unresolved, non-conflict fields
verdicts.reason: native_pipeline.py:456-458 and :39-51 (_progress_state adds recognized keys from every reading, plus statuses) match the claim. image_fusion.py:183 makes conflict permanent. tests/test_native_conflict_pipeline.py:357-372 asserts frames[:5]. comparison.json: 0015 phase1 has 5 views, 34 requests and 26 agent calls; main read 9/20/15/9 views on 0012-0015 against 2/2/2/5 in phase1, with the same confirmed counts 0/2/0/2. verdicts.title: Stop the single-frame search once only conflict fields remain: one fresh view, then the final review
verdicts.reason: native_pipeline.py:919-922 resets disagreements_preserved to None. _stop_reason :165-166 returns it only when every unconfirmed field is conflict. :606-620 builds per-key groups, :229-245 and :630-633 block coverage beyond 4 frames, :1026-1028 sets the exhaustion labels. tests :80-95 assert that all frames are seen. verdicts.title: Make the joint-review answer as compact as the phase1 single-frame answer
verdicts.reason: The citations check out: image_conflicts.py:163 (evidence_text max 4000, 'role/caption and value'), the resolution_reason max_length 2000 in _FieldReview, INSTRUCTIONS 'В evidence_text копируй ... дословно, включая продолжение адреса', image_reader.py:125-127, and the A/B README ('69% of model time'). verdicts.title: Remove over-broad blockers that keep requires_other_document_side from firing
verdicts.reason: The cited guards exist: native_pipeline.py:810 (document.errors), :813 (failed or stopped attempts), :823 (source_reading_count), :827-829 (reading.errors). image_reader.py:376 has the unprefixed heading error and :413 the `name: rejection` format. image_agent.py:229 raises ViewBudgetExceeded, and a generic Exception is caught at :940 as status=failed. verdicts.reason: native_pipeline.py:626 flattens all fields' groups into one list. choose() at :229-245 returns None unless every group, plus the fresh-frame group in the final phase, fits in 4 frames. :251-254 then falls back to candidates[:4], quality-ranked with the fresh frame first. :630-633 blocks fields per frame set. tests :327 cover the blocked case. verdicts.reason: 'The only gap that matches evaluation is ё/е' is wrong. sever/normalize.py strips a leading № on numbers (:10-11, :28-29). It canonicalises date forms, including '20 августа 2026' to ISO (:13-27). For party fields, comparison() at :43-55 folds legal-form expansions, drops quotes and folds punctuation. missing: Segmentation misses (8/20 target intervals) are the largest accuracy loss, and no finding addresses video.py or registration.

Generation is 69% of model time at 61 tok/s single-stream. Batched decode (llama-server --parallel N with the existing opt-in leaf concurrency) and the faster MoE model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: 156.8 s vs 231.2 s on one clip, same 9/10 fields) are likely bigger speed levers than any per-call prompt change, and the report omits both.
Findings 1 and 2 both claim the 0015 savings, so their speed effects cannot be added.

No per-kind token or seconds breakdown exists locally (comparison.json has call counts per leaf only). The per-joint-call seconds in findings 1, 4 and 5 are back-calculated assumptions; compare_runs should add per-kind tokens and timings before ranking.
Reviewing only 4-5 leaves on one video (22 labels, 95% CI about 50-87%) cannot show precision neutrality. The other 10 videos have not been A/B'd on phase1.
Joint-review prefix-cache behaviour: each review sends up to 4 new full images, so its input is largely uncached. Input cost per joint call is not analysed.
No finding addresses the known role-confusion (creator vs consignor) and address-boundary error classes, which are accuracy issues independent of call count.

verdicts.title: Correct the missed-interval metric: 1 of 20 targets missed (not 8), and that miss is a boundary artifact

My replay of the strict matcher (evaluation.py:108) on the 88 primaries in analysis/selected-frame-usability-full.json found 7 misses: video 4 pages 007, 012, 023, 027, 030 and 032, all unknown; video 5 page-005, a TTN with 4 labelled fields. It also found 6+1 unmatched primaries, matching the truth's unmatched_selected_frame_review_indices. verdicts.title: Pick the primary frame from inner, turn-free samples (the current score is noise and favours leaf edges)
verdicts.reason: The cited code matches. video.py:482 limits neighbours to the same leaf, :484 is the score formula, :414 has algorithm_version 4, and :87-94 computes sharpness over the masked paper. On output/accuracy-review/video4-segmentation-observed.json: 26 of 51 primaries in leaves with 3 or more samples sit at the first or last sample (19.5 expected); the median score spread among retained frames is 0.039; the page-0003 primary frame-000027 at 13.86 s has Laplacian variance 1580.6, against 1489.9 and 1465.7 for the earlier samples. Of the 7 unmatched primaries, v4 page-0007/0022/0029 and v5 page-0005 each sit about 0.27 s before their leaf end (one half step), so they are last samples. That the v4 page-0045 primary is the first sample is plausible but not proven. Video 5 leaf page-0005 [18.93, 21.59] has inner samples at about 19.7-20.8 s, inside truth [19.109, 21.174).

verdicts.title: Make the confirming second view independent of the primary, not its closest twin
verdicts.reason: video.py:496-498 multiplies the seed score by minimum_edge_agreement, and :502 sorts by -score and then time proximity. frame_pool.py:133 computes novelty, which only reaches the output field primary_image_difference at :145; :135-136 score = relative_quality*strength, even though the docstring at :167 claims 'quality/novelty order'. In comparison.json, phase1 read 2 views on 14 of 15 leaves (only page-0015 read 5). In the interim v4 segmentation, 39 of 54 first seeds are the adjacent sample, with median mean_abs_difference 0.052. analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:39 records the Кашириных/Каширных glyph difference.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Also note that native_pipeline.py:429-432 orders the seeds by relative_selection_score, which leaves out the strength term. Changing seed selection alone does not decide which seed is read second; the read order must change too. The precision effect is unmeasured.

verdicts.title: Cut spurious short leaves: confirm 2-sample leaves too, and recognise a covered part of the same sheet
verdicts.reason: video.py:291 skips leaves that are not singletons. :141-144 the worst direction decides alone, with a .18 partial threshold. :267-272 two matching pending samples open a new leaf. My strict replay of video4-segmentation-observed.json: 69 leaves, 19 unmatched, 13 of them singletons. The five unmatched inside targets are page-0005 (004 upd), page-0008 (006 ttn), and page-0010/0011/0013 (008 ttn). analysis/accuracy-speed-v8-progress.json:54-64 matches (69/53/15/57).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Three corrections. First, video.py:342-349 already merges kept groups across gaps that hold only rejected samples, so (c) should extend that step, not add a new one. Second, 'labelled precision unchanged' is not guaranteed: the strict matcher takes the primary closest to the interval midpoint, so a fragment can take the match from the real leaf, and removing fragments could change scores. Third, the fragment counts come from the pre-fix interim segmentation; the current code's count is unmeasured.

verdicts.title: Detect repeat showings offline (CPU); use them to save reads only after the customer agrees
verdicts.reason: The truth repeat_of links match (truth lines 584, 727, 1354, 1517, 4232, 4375, 4496, 5096, 5257). The phase1 repeat-leaf seconds 54.63+59.36+109.1+107.57+301.33 = 632 s are confirmed from comparison.json. video.py:182 is the .075 gate. My CPU re-run of sever.video._pair_evidence on PIL-resized analysis/sample-0x/selected-frames originals did not reproduce the key negative. sample-04 original-01 vs original-04 (UPD front vs repeat) came out same_page True: 108 inliers, fraction .079, coverage .638. The report has False: 99 inliers, fraction .072. The sample-05 UPD pair was True (249 inliers, coverage .40), and the sample-05 TTN pair 02 vs 05 was also True.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The repeat pair sits right at the .075 inlier-fraction gate, so the outcome depends on the resize/decode path. 'The gate misses real repeats' is fragile rather than shown. A dedicated rule is still reasonable, but its margin needs measuring on pipeline thumbnails. Reusing an earlier leaf's confirmed reading also stretches the per-leaf two-frame rule (README.md:38, :98), as the report says.

verdicts.title: Re-rank seeds and pool frames by quality inside the unresolved fields' regions (not glare in this footage)
verdicts.reason: frame_pool.py:128-138 ranks once by thumbnail sharpness x strength. :69 scale=384:-2 -q:v 5 is a 2160/384 = 5.6x downscale. video.py:163 computes the homography but :189-193 does not return it. video.py:87 drops the top 18%. schema.py:21 has bbox. image_reader.py:370 and image_agent.py:164 store the crop/panel bbox normalized to the saved source frame. On the 174 frames of video4-segmentation-observed.json, the maximum maximum_local_near_white_fraction is 0.000156 and only 4 frames have skin > 0.1. In comparison.json the pool ran only on phase1 page-0015 (5 views, 301 s) and on main 0012-0015 (9-20 views).
verdicts.corrected_claim: The evidence bbox is the model-chosen crop/panel region, not a field box. The homography lives in the coordinates of the cropped (top 18%, sides 3.5%) 384-px thumbnail, and pool candidates are registered only against the primary. Mapping a bbox read from a seed needs chained transforms, and header fields in the top 18% fall outside the registered region. The speed and precision gains are unmeasured.

verdicts.title: Offline segmentation scorer and cached-feature parameter sweep (no model calls)
verdicts.reason: Every cited threshold line checks out: video.py:135 (100/.55), :144 (.18), :154 (.72), :182 (16/.075/.08), :186-188 (.22/.90/.05, .11), :244 (20 keypoints / .25 bright), :289 radius, :326 hull .2, :332 span .12. evaluation.py:89-114 needs only pages and primary timestamps, plus result.source.sha256 to pass the hash check. The truth has boundary_uncertainty for videos 4 and 5 only; videos 1 and 2 have stable_window or null. accuracy-speed-v8-progress.json:64 gives 95 s.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Bracket ranges exist only for sample-04 and sample-05; sample-01 and sample-02 must use strict mode. The scorer needs to supply the source sha256, because video-analysis.json does not carry it.

verdicts.title: Overlap CPU video work with model reading
verdicts.reason: The code claims are right. video.py:443 is the first full decode, :531-533 a second full decode by PTS with no seek, and :300-308 a seeked probe per singleton. native_pipeline.py:415-419 calls next() synchronously unless leaf_concurrency>1, and :802-807 shows the iterator includes the frame_pool factory. The savings are unmeasured. 95 s/53 truth intervals is about 1.8 s per sheet. The pool runs on only 1 of 15 phase1 leaves, so prefetching it saves almost nothing.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Most of the gain would come from streaming or seeked original extraction, not from pool prefetch. Leaf boundaries depend on the next group's first sample, and short candidates need dense confirmation, so streaming needs at least a one-leaf lag. The gain stays about 2-4% and is unverified.

verdicts.title: Effective base sampling is 0.533 s; do not move the base to 0.25 s
verdicts.reason: video.py:442 uses gte(t-prev_selected_t, 0.5). With 30.01 fps, 15 frames is 0.49980 s, below 0.5, so each step is 16 frames = 0.53312 s. 345 samples over 183.66 s is 0.532 s. The shortest target, sample-04-page-011 (1.53 s), was matched in my strict replay. The only target miss, sample-05-page-005 (2.07 s), is a boundary artifact. The truth inventory_limit text says very brief, fully covered showings cannot be ruled out.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Under bracket matching, which video-4 non-target interval stays unmatched (012 blank reverse or 013 EAC declaration) depends on the tie-break. Neither is a sampling loss. The CPU cost of 0.25 s sampling is an estimate.

missing: The V7 segmentation itself (87 leaves, implied by 8 misses and 7 unmatched) was never replayed. The report's per-video split of the 8 misses (6/1/1) is a forecast. /root/sever-validation/native-v7-evaluation/finish-evaluation.json should be read before the '1 of 20 targets' claim is published.

Several statistics (primary first/last rate, seed adjacency, fragment counts) come from output/accuracy-review/video4-segmentation-observed.json. That file is algorithm_version 3 with max_pages 300, an interim segmentation, not today's algorithm_version 4 code.

The strict matcher picks the primary closest to the interval midpoint, so extra fragments can take matches from the real leaf. Segmentation changes can therefore move the labelled metrics even though one-to-one matching ignores extras.

native_pipeline.py:429-432 orders seeds by relative_selection_score, while video.py:502 selects them by score x edge agreement. The first seed read and the top-ranked seed can differ, so any seed-selection fix must also cover the read order.
video.py:342-349 already merges kept groups across gaps that hold only rejected samples. Proposals for merging short candidates should build on it.

For videos 4 and 5, bracket windows overlap their neighbours by about 1-1.5 s, so a 2 s interval can accept primaries from a 3 s window. The extra metric should report how many matches depend on that overlap only.
The repeat-link gate result depends on how thumbnails are produced (ffmpeg -q:v 5 vs PIL resize). Regression tests built from the selected-frames JPEGs may not represent pipeline thumbnails.

verdicts.title: Benchmark Qwen3.6-27B as a drop-in replacement for Qwen3.8-27B (same architecture, better Russian OCR and extraction)
verdicts.reason: All cited numbers check out. MWS-Vision-Bench test (private): Qwen3.6-27B 0.692/0.861/0.753/0.062/0.893 vs Qwen3.8-27B 0.687/0.797/0.738/0.223/0.807 (https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench). Validation split shows the same order (OCR 0.863 vs 0.800). OCRBench v2 2026.09 EN: 68.3 (#5) vs 63.5 (#11) (https://99franklin.github.io/ocrbench_v2/). Qwen3.8 card: OSWorld-Verified 84.3 vs 63.9, OmniDocBench 1.5 91.1 vs 89.4. Both cards describe the same layout: 64 layers in 16 blocks of 3 DeltaNet + 1 gated attention, 4 KV heads x 256 dims. unsloth Qwen3.6-27B-Q6_K is 22.5 GB and mmproj-F16 is 928 MB. MWS says nothing about thinking mode or precision, which matches the stated risk. Caveats: the Qwen3.8 card says it beats Qwen3.6-27B on every shared benchmark, so the Russian edge rests on one third-party benchmark. Linking the glyph errors to the OCR axis is a guess. zoom_regions takes model-emitted normalized boxes (sever/image_agent.py:75,302), so the grounding risk is real.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Supported as a cheap A/B. The OCR/KIE lead comes from one third-party benchmark (MWS), whose thinking and precision settings are unknown. Qwen's own card shows Qwen3.8 ahead everywhere it compares the two. Note that the user chose Qwen3.8-27B on purpose (deploy/README.md:260).

verdicts.title: Benchmark Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE) for speed: workload is prompt-processing-bound
verdicts.reason: The 'prompt-processing-bound' reasoning is contradicted by the project's own server timings. In analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.md:47 (phase1-speed, 188 responses), 639,726 uncached input tokens took 273.4 s, while 41,696 output tokens took 688.5 s. Decoding is about 69% of the 1004 s model time (about 60 tok/s); prompt processing is about 27%. llama.cpp already serves about 68% of input tokens from cache (1,352,407 cached). The model-card facts are confirmed: 35B total / 3B active; 40 layers = 10 x (3 DeltaNet + 1 attention); 2 KV heads x 256; 256 experts with 8 routed + 1 shared; OmniDocBench1.5 89.9, CC-OCR 81.9; vLLM 0.19.0 / SGLang 0.5.10 (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). MWS row 0.691/0.847/0.755/0.094/0.840 is confirmed. GGUF sizes are confirmed: UD-Q4_K_XL 22.4, UD-Q5_K_M 26.5, UD-Q6_K 29.3, MXFP4_MOE 21.7 GB, mmproj-F16 899 MB. The '156.8 vs 231.2 s on one clip' trial was actually two short clips run on the older OCR->classification->reading pipeline before the v6 fix, not native_image (README.md:78). Also, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6 already ran on this 32 GB server (deploy/README.md:241,260), which undercuts the claim that Q6 is too tight.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Worth benchmarking, but because the workload is decode-bound, not prefill-bound. About 69% of model time is generating about 222 tokens per call at about 60 tok/s. A 3B-active MoE reads far fewer weight bytes per output token, so decode speedups could exceed the 1.3–2x estimate. The prior 1.48x figure came from the old pipeline on two clips. Q6 has already run on this GPU.

verdicts.title: Check prefix-cache reuse for hybrid DeltaNet models on llama.cpp; vLLM is the fallback
verdicts.reason: The citations exist, but the premise does not hold for this workload. llama.cpp#22384 was closed as completed by ggerganov on 2026-04-26 with 'The fix is incorrect. There is nothing to fix in llama-server'. The reporter says reprocessing persists in b8943 with Qwen3.6-27B. The candidate table's 'open complaint' wording is wrong. The v2ex thread is confirmed: 19K prompt vs checkpoints at 39K–71K, full reprocess. Friendli confirmed: default vLLM prefix caching is only 79%. The 99% figure needs --prefix-match-unit 16 with MTP off, and 93–98% needs MTP K=2 + prefix-match-unit; weights 18.2 GB, vision BF16. HivenetQuant NVFP4 confirmed (vision BF16, RTX 5090 benchmarks). But the project's own data shows llama.cpp already caches about 68% of input tokens (comparison.md:47: cached 1.35M vs processed 0.64M), and all prompt processing together is only 273 s of 1004 s model time. Perfect caching could save at most about 27% of model time, so 'any regression directly multiplies' and 'cut prompt-processing time substantially' are overstated. The proposed check is already answerable from existing server_timings in analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.json.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Low priority. llama.cpp prefix reuse already gives about 68% cache hits, close to vLLM's default 79%. Prompt processing is about 27% of model time, so a stack switch for caching alone can recover at most about a quarter of model time. vLLM is more interesting for MTP/batching than for prefix caching.

verdicts.title: F7: crop-level second reading with OCR, and F8: OCR fingerprints for missed intervals
verdicts.reason: The supporting citations hold: dots.ocr prompt_grounding_ocr; PR 18825 recommends layout first then recognizing regions; sever/image_reader.py:2-4; sever/image_fusion.py:109; sever/video.py:405; sever/ocr.py:286 _header_line_boxes. The benefits are speculative and unmeasured, and F8 depends on the unknown failure mode of the 8 missed intervals.

missing: None of the proxy benchmarks measures what the product needs. GlotOCR uses rendered synthetic sentence images; MDPBench and OmniDocBench are page-level edit distance or parsing scores. None tests key-value extraction or literal field accuracy on photographed Russian forms. Real5 is published by PaddlePaddle, so it has the same self-evaluation bias the report flags only for MDPBench.

Classic Cyrillic OCR baselines with line boxes are missing beyond PP-OCRv5: Surya (strong Russian, line bboxes; its licence restricts commercial use), docTR, EasyOCR, and the Tesseract rus engine the server already falls back to (sever/ocr.py:324-326). The bake-off should include the existing Tesseract path as the zero-cost baseline.

On the Linux server, sever/ocr.py uses tesseract_rus_eng; Apple Vision runs only on macOS. It also writes an OCR cache (_write_cache). Reusing it would conflict with the 'stored model answers are never replayed' rule, and the report did not check this.

Prefix-cache interaction: about 73% of input tokens are llama.cpp prefix-cache reads today. Adding per-frame OCR hint text (F2) must go after the static ~24k-char instructions and schema, or it invalidates the cache and raises prefill time. This could offset the speed gain.

GPU contention under the existing shared inference lock and --parallel 1. A second OCR server on the same RTX 5090 would make the phase1-speed A/B timings incomparable unless both arms run with it, and the report does not quantify the slowdown to the 27B.

Cheaper speed levers that need no new model are not compared against OCR: lowering --image-max-tokens or the zoom-crop resolution, or switching to the already-tried Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE for the field agent. They give a baseline the OCR proposals must beat.
General VLMs with native text grounding or spotting (e.g. Qwen-VL family OCR or grounding modes in the model already deployed) are not considered. They could supply line boxes without a second model.

Licence detail for HunyuanOCR: the Tencent Hunyuan Community License territory clause (it excludes the EU, UK and South Korea) and its user-count thresholds. The report only says to check it; whether Russia-based commercial use is allowed should be confirmed.

The 2160x3840 frames are portrait 8.3 MP. Most of these OCR models were benchmarked at ~1540–2048 px long edge, so the bake-off must also test resizing and tiling choices, which affect both speed and Cyrillic accuracy.

verdicts.title: Check whether each view's first request misses the prefix cache (hybrid model + one slot) and shrink what a miss costs
verdicts.reason: The citations are accurate: zoom_image_reader.py:49-50, 72-73 and 86-87; the address rule five times (image_reader.py:54-56, 59-68, 132-135, 175, 177); «он же» at 44-50, 137-140 and 174; README.md:20 and :23. 168k/2,340 tok/s is about 72 s. But the premise 'three different system prompts in a row per view' is wrong for phase1. Orientation is reused per leaf (zoom_image_reader.py:41-46), and triage runs only until full_read_required (:70); comparison.json has 15 orientation and 19 triage calls over 25 field-agent views. So for a leaf's second view, the request just before is usually the previous view's last field-agent request, with the same instructions and tools. A miss on that view can only come from hybrid/recurrent rollback limits. The 'looks hybrid' inference from 26 GB of GPU memory is a guess and not shown. The checkpoint mechanism and the --checkpoint-min-step default of 8192 do exist in a local llama.cpp build (common/common.h:620-621, server-context.cpp:3264,3344-3357), but that is not the server's v0.6.0 build. verdicts.title: Remove 'conflict' from the per-frame field status: one such answer permanently blocks two-frame confirmation
verdicts.reason: schema.py:7 includes 'conflict', and ImageField.status uses it (image_reader.py:162). _validate_reading keeps a conflict with null raw_value unchanged (:407-411). In image_fusion.py:181-185, any per-frame conflict with frame evidence makes the fused field 'conflict'. native_pipeline.py:165-166 does count conflict toward 'disagreements_preserved', but the loop resets that stop to None (:919-922), so the leaf keeps reading, as claimed. INSTRUCTIONS and ZOOM_INSTRUCTIONS never define a per-frame conflict. Two nuances. First, 'permanently' is too strong: a joint review can still resolve the field (fresh_joint_model_review, native_pipeline.py:552-554). Second, a later per-frame 'conflict' also invalidates an earlier joint resolution (:536-547), which makes the finding stronger. Joint review reuses UPDFields etc. (image_conflicts.py:24-25,33) and also treats a 'conflict' status as an explicit disagreement (:159, :296), so the risk the finding states is real.

Segmentation misses (8/20 target intervals) are the biggest accuracy loss, and no reading-side change addresses them. The expected precision gains should be weighed against this.
observed_form is shown in the HTML report for every reading (report.py:312) and stored per attempt (native_pipeline.py:902). Dropping it for supported forms changes the report.

Band panels make evidence bounding boxes much coarser (half a sheet per panel). This should be checked against how evidence is presented to the customer.
The report does not reconcile its two schema token counts (3,435 vs 3,567) or say which serialization the server actually receives.

The context facts call phase1-speed 'unmeasured', but analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md records a measured A/B: 1,134 s, 15/22 fields. The findings rely on that one run; with 22 labels the 95% interval spans roughly 50-87%, so precision claims cannot be settled on video 5 alone.

verdicts.title: Enable MTP speculative decoding on the existing Qwen3.8-27B GGUF
verdicts.reason: PR https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/22673 is merged (May 16, 2026). It states "MTP is compatible with Vision input" and warns "Prompt processing (PP) speed typically takes a negative hit". The 5090 27B q4_0 figures 63.72 -> 105.47 tok/s (acceptance 0.797) come from a commenter running draft 3. The n_parallel=1 error is quoted in a comment. The server README --spec-type list includes draft-mtp, and --spec-draft-n-max defaults to 3. In HF discussions/14 (UD-Q6_K_XL) the no-vision/no-MTP run is about 52-56 tok/s and vision+MTP is about 92 tok/s, but the 92 was measured at n-max 5. The n-max sweep (1.47x at n-max 1, 1.51x at n-max 2) is UD-Q4_K_XL on code, and n-max 6 was slower only on prose. The 1315 -> 665 prefill drop is in the PR thread (3090+3060), not in the HF thread. Unsloth doc: 'MTP enabled', '1-2GB extra headroom'. #22867 (MTP+vision slot corruption) was closed May 10, 2026, but the page names no upstream fix PR, only a fork PR (am17an#5). Repo: README 22-23 gives 688 s / 61 tok/s / 69%, and the service file has no --spec-type.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The ~92 tok/s vision+MTP figure was measured at --spec-draft-n-max 5 (UD-Q6_K_XL, 65k ctx), not 2. The n-max 1 vs 2 vs 6 sweep was on UD-Q4_K_XL, and only n-max 6 on prose fell below baseline. So the n-max that is best here is unknown; sweep 1-3 (the default is 3). The prefill-halving report (1315 -> 665) is from the llama.cpp PR thread on a 3090+3060 setup. Whether the #22867 fix is upstream is unconfirmed, so check the build.

verdicts.title: Keep the tool list constant within a run so the cache survives
verdicts.reason: sever/image_agent.py:256-265 prepare_zoom returns None when zoom_count>=8 or requests_started>=7, and the comment at 278-280 says 'the next model request exposes only the submission tool'. image_conflicts.py:461-465 uses the same pattern. Pydantic docs: prepare can 'return None to omit the tool for that step'. The Qwen3.8 chat_template.jinja emits '<|im_start|>system\n', then '# Tools ... <tools>' ... '</tools>', then the tool-call instructions, and only then the system content, so the prefix diverges within the first ~10-20 tokens. PR #20087 says 'once any prefix is invalid, you have to reprocess', and #18497 confirms the recurrent-state reasoning. Caveat: a change this early forces full reprocessing on any model, hybrid or not. Also, the decline text at image_agent.py:288 already says 'Submit using the supplied pixels', so adding 'submit now' is redundant. How often this happens is not measured.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Removing tools changes the prompt about 10-20 tokens in, so the whole request is re-processed on any architecture; the hybrid-checkpoint argument is not needed. The existing decline message already tells the model to submit. How often it happens is unmeasured.

verdicts.title: Space hybrid-model checkpoints so the shared prefix is reused across frames
verdicts.reason: The flags match the llama.cpp server README: -cms/--checkpoint-min-step default 8192 (0 = no minimum), --ctx-checkpoints default 32, --cache-ram default 8192, --cache-idle-slots 'default: enabled, requires cache-ram'. Since --cache-ram 8192 and idle-slot saving are already the defaults, the 'keep' advice changes nothing. #18497 and PR #20087 support the mechanism. The lmstudio #1818 figures (60K repeat prompt ~70-80 s -> ~1.0 s) are real, but they were on Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B with --checkpoint-every-n-tokens 4096 / --ctx-checkpoints 128 / --swa-full, not Qwen3.8. Roboflow confirms 64 layers with a 3 DeltaNet : 1 attention pattern. The central claim, that each field-agent run re-processes the ~8k prefix, is the author's estimate and has not been measured; 68% of input tokens are already cache hits. Different call types also have different tool lists, so they share almost no prefix anyway.
verdicts.corrected_claim: This is a plausible but unmeasured hypothesis. Measure cache_n at the start of each field-agent run before changing flags. --cache-ram 8192 and --cache-idle-slots are already the defaults.

verdicts.title: Let the client set image sizes: send real 768x1376 contexts and stop server-side upscaling of crops
verdicts.reason: mtmd-image.cpp contains `else if (opts.min_pixels > 0 && h_bar * w_bar < opts.min_pixels)`, which scales up by beta=sqrt(min/hw) and uses ceil_by_factor with align_size = patch_size*n_merge. The Qwen3.8 preprocessor_config shows patch_size 16, merge_size 2, shortest_edge 65536, longest_edge 16777216. The Qwen3-VL README says 'compression ratio is 32' and gives the 256*32*32 / 1280*32*32 example. The arithmetic checks out: 576x1024 -> 768x1376 = 1032 tokens; 1080x230 -> 2240x480 = 1050 tokens; 2160x3840 under 4096 tokens -> 1536x2720 = 4080. Repo: service file sets min 1024/max 4096; image_agent.py:141 thumbnails to 1024 with Lanczos; image_agent.py:77 says 'without magnification'; README.md:213 says 'без изменения нативного масштаба'. The estimate of 150-200 crops per video is not measured.

verdicts.title: Send homography-mapped crops in the first request for later frames of the same sheet
verdicts.reason: sever/video.py:163 calls cv2.findHomography(pb, pa, cv2.RANSAC, 3.5), and the matrix is not stored. comparison.md shows 115 field_agent calls. arXiv 2609.22910 ('When Should a VLM Look?', 19 Sep 2026) abstract: 'only 10% to 12% of visual calls were both needed and used', spurious calls '36% to 87% of the time'. The 'cold start' qualifier was not checked. The 2505.21333 abstract says 'limited capability' on holistic video comprehension and cross-frame integration. The speed estimate is unmeasured. The business-rule risk is understated: the rectangles are part of frame 1's stored model answer, and README forbids replaying stored model answers.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The sources are accurate. Reusing frame-1 model-chosen rectangles as frame-k input is arguably a reuse of a stored model answer as well as an independence issue. Get explicit customer sign-off before building it.

verdicts.title: Pick frames by per-region sharpness; avoid multi-frame super-resolution
verdicts.reason: sever/frame_pool.py:128-136 ranks by whole-frame sharpness_laplacian_variance. quality.py:63 lists 'sharp_background_or_page_edges_can_hide_blurred_text'. Q-Frame (arXiv 2506.22139v3, 22 Jul 2025) Table 11: Video-MME OCR 56.8 -> 68.3 for Qwen2-VL-7B without subtitles (65.5 -> 67.6 with subtitles). Q-Frame does query-aware frame selection plus multi-resolution, which is close to the report's description. No speed or precision numbers are claimed.

verdicts.title: Deskew or rectify the context and crops with a 4-corner homography; use learned dewarping only for curled sheets
verdicts.reason: TeleOCR (arXiv 2608.12898v3, 10 Sep 2026) states 'removing geometric distortions alone substantially improves two-stage parsing performance', and Table 3 gives Qwen3-VL-8B Clean 72.44 vs Real Degraded 62.73. ForCenNet (2507.19804, ICCV 2025 per CVF open access) Table 1 lists CER 0.136 vs DocTr 0.183, DocGeoNet 0.182, FTDR 0.170, CGU-Net(UVDoc) 0.178 with ED 513.76; that ED is better than ForCenNet's 571.40. PaddleOCR lists UVDoc CER 0.179, 30.3 MB, 19.05 ms on a T4. 2501.03145 v3 (15 Nov 2025) uses YOLOv8 masks plus a cubic polynomial grid with median CER 0.0235. Nuance: TeleOCR does not itself use ForCenNet as an inference preprocessor; it cites it for a motivating dewarping experiment and for synthesizing deformations, and it explicitly avoids a dewarping module. README.md:38 'Отдельного классификатора...' confirmed.
verdicts.corrected_claim: TeleOCR cites ForCenNet for its dewarping experiment and data synthesis. It does not use ForCenNet as its preprocessor, and its method avoids a separate dewarping module. ForCenNet does not have the best ED on DocUNet; CGU-Net/UVDoc does.

verdicts.title: Try Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE) as the decode-speed option
verdicts.reason: Zenn article: RTX 5090, llama.cpp b8870, UD-Q5_K_S PP512 3293 / TG128 180, UD-Q4_K_M 2892 / 183, 23.2 GB file and about 25 GB VRAM. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B README: 35B total / 3B active, Apache-2.0, OmniDocBench1.5 89.9, CC-OCR 81.9, CharXiv RQ 78.0, vLLM method qwen3_next_mtp. Qwen3.8-27B README: OmniDocBench1.5 91.1. README.md:78 confirms 9/10 at 156.83 s vs 231.19 s, but that run used the old OCR-guided pipeline, and the README says it is 'не независимо измеренная точность'. deploy/README.md:260 says 'Выбранная пользователем'. Caveats: '3x' compares llama-bench tg128 at empty context with 61 tok/s measured in production at ~10k context. 'MTP works with it in llama.cpp' was not verified on the PR page.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The ~3x decode figure compares an empty-context llama-bench with production at ~10k context, so expect less. The 9/10-field parity comes from the obsolete OCR-guided pipeline, not native_image.

verdicts.title: A/B two parallel slots with a unified KV pool against MTP
verdicts.reason: The server README describes -kvu/--kv-unified ('default: enabled if number of slots is auto', so it must be passed explicitly with --parallel 2) and --kv-unified-per-slot. The PR #22673 comment quotes 'MTP currently supports only n_parallel=1'. deploy/README.md:588-590 confirms the context is split per slot. The 1.5-1.9x figure is unsourced, as the report says.

verdicts.title: Remove or shrink the orientation call
verdicts.reason: image_detail.py:88 thumbnails non-native panels to 1024. image_orientation.py:55-80 sends four rotated contexts in one call. comparison.md lists 15 orientation calls. PaddleOCR doc_preprocessor gives PP-LCNet_x1_0_doc_ori 99.06% top-1 (self-built PaddleX set of 1,000 images), 2.62/0.59 ms on GPU, 7 MB. The page does not state a 224x224 input size. README.md:38 states there is no separate classifier. The 288x512 = 144-token figure only holds after min-tokens is lowered, as the report notes. The insufficient_evidence re-pick claim was not checked.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The 224x224 input size for PP-LCNet_x1_0_doc_ori is not stated on the cited page.

verdicts.title: Fewer output tokens: integer 0-1000 zoom coordinates and per-step max_tokens caps
verdicts.reason: Repo checks out: image_agent.py:36 defines a float Coordinate in [0,1], and image_agent.py:328 sets max_tokens from effective.max_output_tokens (8192). The Qwen3-VL README says only 'relative position coordinates' and gives no range. Issue #1616 is a Qwen2.5-VL / LLaMA-Factory question; in it, user HumanZhong (affiliation unknown) recommends 0-1000 boxes for Qwen3-VL. Nothing documents what Qwen3.8 uses. The token savings were not verified, and the report itself rates confidence at 0.3.

verdicts.title: Constrained JSON / grammar sampling is not the bottleneck
verdicts.reason: The citations check out. The grammars README warns 'x? x? x?.... x? ... may result in extremely slow sampling' and says additionalProperties false 'produces faster grammars'. llguidance.md gives '50μs of single-core CPU time' and p99 0.5ms. #4218 (titled 'llama : speed-up grammar sampling') contains the quoted line in a comment by ejones. image_reader.py:161-167 shows the max_length values. The inference does not hold: 61 tok/s in production (with vision, ~10k context, possibly lazy tool-call grammar) is compared with 52-56 tok/s from a different user's setup (no vision, 208k ctx config). That cannot isolate grammar overhead, and it has not been shown that a grammar is active at all for Qwen XML tool calls with tool_choice auto.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The evidence does not yet show whether grammar overhead matters. Decide only after the proposed llama-bench vs trace predicted_ms comparison.

verdicts.title: Test a larger physical batch (-ub) for prefill
verdicts.reason: The llama.cpp server README states '-ub, --ubatch-size N | physical maximum batch size (default: 512)'. sever-model.service:12 sets no -ub. README gives prefill 273 s at 2,340 tok/s. The report states the effect is unknown, which is accurate.

missing: The largest lever is call count on the 4 hard leaves (72% of calls, 74% of time). The report has no per-leaf call cap, no early stop for conflicts that stay unresolved, and no limit on joint-review rounds; it optimizes mostly per-call speed.
Segmentation misses 8/20 target intervals, the biggest accuracy loss, and no finding addresses it (e.g. denser sampling, a looser ORB/RANSAC grouping threshold, an analysis of missed intervals).
Decode is bandwidth-bound, so a smaller quant of the same 27B model (Q5_K/Q4_K_M) is a cheap ~1.2-1.4x decode option. It was not considered, and it would need an accuracy A/B.
The K/V cache type (q8_0 vs f16) affects decode speed with flash-attn; this was not tested.
vLLM/SGLang (both listed on the Qwen3.8 card) support MTP together with concurrent requests and prefix caching. That would remove llama.cpp's MTP-or-parallel trade-off.

The deployed build is labelled 'v0.6.0', which is not a normal llama.cpp bNNNN tag. Every flag proposal (draft-mtp, -cms, --kv-unified-per-slot) depends on that build being newer than May 2026; check `llama-server --help` first.

Several findings may affect accuracy (image sizes, deskew, mapped crops, caps), but only 44 provisional labels exist (22 on video 5). That is too few to detect small regressions. Expand the labels before trusting precision A/Bs.
How speculative decoding interacts with grammar-constrained tool-call sampling, and how acceptance rate varies with JSON/XML output, was not considered.
Reusing frame-1 model-chosen rectangles may conflict with the 'stored model answers are never replayed' rule, not only with frame independence.

verdicts.title: Ceiling estimate: on Russian KIE, local 27B-class Qwen is already close to hosted frontier models; segmentation, not the reader model, is the main loss
verdicts.reason: The MWS rows match the page exactly (test: GPT-5.6 Sol 0.789/0.836/0.862/0.623; Cotype Pro 3 KIE 0.906; Claude Sonnet 5 KIE 0.830; Gemini 3.5 Flash 0.882; Qwen3.6-27B 0.893; Qwen3.8-27B 0.807/grounding 0.223; validation: Opus 5.5 0.896, Gemini 3.6 Flash 0.903, GPT-6.1 Sol 0.822). The page gives no KIE formula and no inference settings. Three framing claims fail. (1) Hosted KIE on test runs 0.818 to 0.906, not 0.86 to 0.91: Sonnet 5 is 0.830 and GPT-6 Luna 0.818. (2) Best KIE minus deployed Qwen3.8-27B is about 9.9 points on test (Cotype Pro 3 0.906 vs 0.807), so 'at most 5-9' is low. Qwen3.6-27B alone is 8.6 points above the deployed model, so the deployed reader is not near ceiling. (3) analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:37-38 says that on video 5 'labelled intervals detected 14/15 both', yet 6-7 of 22 fields were wrong. On that video segmentation is not the main loss. The 8/20 figure is a 4-video aggregate.
verdicts.corrected_claim: On MWS private test, hosted KIE runs 0.818-0.906. The open Qwen3.6-27B (0.893) matches or beats most hosted models, but the deployed Qwen3.8-27B (0.807) is about 9-10 points below the best. Segmentation is the largest loss only in the 4-video aggregate. On video 5 (14/15 intervals detected) most errors are other-side, label-boundary or reader errors.

verdicts.title: A/B Qwen3.6-27B against the deployed Qwen3.8-27B: better Russian text reading and KIE, much weaker grounding
verdicts.reason: MWS test and validation rows match verbatim: 3.8-27B 0.687/0.797/0.738/0.223/0.807/0.873 and 3.6-27B 0.692/0.861/0.753/0.062/0.893/0.889; validation img→text 0.863 vs 0.800, KIE 0.833 vs 0.812. OCRBench v2 2026.09 matches: English 68.3 vs 63.5, Recognition 71.1 vs 75.5, Extraction 92.8 vs 90.4; Chinese 58.7 vs 56.9. The Qwen3.8-27B card gives OmniDocBench 1.5 91.1 vs 89.4 and OSWorld-Verified 84.3 vs 63.9. Both cards give 64 layers in a 16×(3 DeltaNet + 1 attention) layout. deploy/sever-model.service:12 uses ${MODEL_PATH}/${MMPROJ_PATH}. One correction: the 'Unsloth notes mmproj not interchangeable' attribution is not on unsloth.ai/docs/models/qwen3.6. Only a third-party site (allthings.how) says so. Using the matching mmproj is still correct practice.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Same as stated, except that the mmproj non-interchangeability note comes from allthings.how, not Unsloth. Also, the MWS validation/test KIE gap for Qwen3.6-27B (0.833 vs 0.893) is as large as the gap between the two models.

verdicts.title: Use the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE, not an 8B model, as the speed option: the pipeline is decode-bound and the MoE does not lose on Russian reading
verdicts.reason: MWS test row 'Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 0.691 | 0.847 | 0.755 | 0.094 | 0.840 | 0.920' matches. OCRBench v2 English 65.5 (Chinese 60.8) matches. The HF card gives OmniDocBench1.5 89.9 and CC-OCR 81.9. Unsloth gives 240 vs 160 tok/s on an RTX 6000, and separately about 220 vs 140. The 140 figure is for the UD-Q2_K_XL quant and both are with MTP, so they do not transfer directly to Q6 without MTP. Unsloth's memory table (6-bit 30 GB, 4-bit 23 GB; 27B 6-bit 24 GB) and the CUDA 13.2 warning match. The README.md:22-23 figures (61 tok/s, 69% of model time) match. The MoE MTP gain is only 1.15-1.2x vs 1.4x for dense, which narrows the MoE advantage once MTP is applied to both.

verdicts.title: Do not downsize to an 8–9B model: it loses 4–10 KIE points on Russian documents and much more on photographed Russian pages
verdicts.reason: The Qwen3.5-27B/9B card values match (88.9/87.7, 81.0/79.3, 89.4/89.2). The MWS rows for Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3-VL-8B match (Qwen3-VL-32B KIE 0.671). The CC-OCR v2 Appendix A.4 quote and the Qwen3.8 collection (only 27B and 2.4T-A95B) are confirmed. The MDPBench numbers are misread: the report took the KO column as RU. Table 2 of arxiv 2603.28130 lists AR,HI,JP,KO,RU,TH,ZH,ZH-T after a Non-Latin Avg. I recomputed that average to check the column positions: (71.3+67.7+69.5+86.0+76.0+68.4+84.8+75.7)/8 = 74.9, as printed. The correct RU values are Qwen3-VL-8B 57.9, Qwen3.5-9B 54.7, Gemini-3-pro 84.9, PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 76.0. The conclusion holds and is stronger.
verdicts.corrected_claim: On MDPBench RU, Qwen3-VL-8B scores 57.9 and Qwen3.5-9B 54.7, vs 84.9 for Gemini-3-pro-preview and 76.0 for PaddleOCR-VL-1.5. The other numbers are as stated.

verdicts.title: Small specialist OCR parsers match Gemini 3 Pro on photographed Russian text; use them at most as a glyph cross-check, not as the field reader
verdicts.reason: The headline is false. In MDPBench Table 2 (arxiv 2603.28130v1), 86.0 is PaddleOCR-VL-1.5's KO score; its RU score is 76.0, vs 84.9 for Gemini-3-pro-preview. The Non-Latin Avg 74.9 checks out with that column order. PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 is not the highest on RU and does not match Gemini on Russian. Other figures check out: Real5-OmniDocBench 92.05/93.19/89.24/78.66 and Qwen3-VL-235B 88.904 (arxiv 2606.03264); Cyrillic edit distance 0.109 vs 0.220 (arxiv 2510.14528); Chandra ru row '88.8% 85.5% 88.7% 82.8% 72.2%' (github.com/datalab-to/chandra). That row shows Chandra 1 (88.7%) beating Chandra 2 (85.5%) on Russian, which the report omits. Real5 measures photographed pages in general, not Russian.
verdicts.corrected_claim: On photographed multilingual pages (Real5-OmniDocBench) PaddleOCR-VL-1.5/1.6 beat Gemini-3 Pro. On Russian (MDPBench RU) PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 scores 76.0, about 9 points behind Gemini-3-pro (84.9), and its Photo score is 75.2. Chandra 1 (88.7%) scores above Chandra 2 (85.5%) on Datalab's ru row. The use as a glyph cross-check only stays reasonable, but the Russian evidence for it is weaker than stated.

verdicts.title: Public OCR benchmarks cannot settle model choice at this label size; grow the labelled set first
verdicts.reason: The LlamaIndex blog (Feb 24 2026) states GLM-OCR at 94.6% and that GLM-OCR and PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 'surpassed 94%'. It says the dataset is small and skewed to academic papers, with no form fields or handwriting. Nanonets omnidocbench page: Qwen3.5-9B 76.7, GPT-5.4 85.3, Gemini-3-Pro 88.8. Codesota: Gemini 3 Pro 90.33, marked unverified. The README.md:43 quote matches. Two parts do not hold up: the 'GPT-5.4 89.1 (another aggregator)' figure has no URL and could not be checked, and the 150+ figure is optimistic. At p≈0.8, a ±5-point 95% half-width needs about 0.16·(1.96/0.05)² ≈ 246 fields; 150 fields give about ±6.4 points.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Same, but resolving ±5 points at 95% needs about 250 labelled fields per model (more for an unpaired comparison). The GPT-5.4 89.1 figure is unsourced.

verdicts.title: Decode-side speedup available on the current model: llama.cpp MTP speculative decoding for Qwen3.6/3.8 hybrids
verdicts.reason: The Unsloth Qwen3.6 page says 'llama.cpp has merged MTP support' and links PR #22673. It gives the flags '--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2', '1.4x for dense models at draft tokens = 2 and for the MoE around 1.15 to 1.2x', acceptance falling from 83% to 50% at 4 draft tokens, and MTP rows needing about 1 GB more. Only the 35B-A3B example includes --mmproj. The Qwen3.8-27B card states 'MTP (Multi-Token Prediction): trained with multiple steps'. Unverified: whether an MTP GGUF exists for Qwen3.8-27B (all Unsloth numbers are for Qwen3.6). Byte-identical output under greedy speculation is likely but not guaranteed in llama.cpp, because batched verification can change floating-point accumulation.

verdicts.title: Russian-specific failure mode: Cyrillic/Latin lookalike letters can pass two-frame fusion unnoticed
verdicts.reason: The report undersells its own source. MDPBench (arxiv 2603.28130v1) says 'For Russian documents, models frequently suffer from visual confusion' and goes on to 'erroneously decoding Cyrillic characters that are visually identical to Latin letters', so the lookalike wording is in the paper. sever/image_fusion.py _literal_comparison is NFKC + casefold + whitespace only, so it does not map homoglyphs. grep finds only the sever/vision.py:1079 comment. No mixed-script check exists.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The MDPBench text itself names Cyrillic characters misread as identical-looking Latin letters as the Russian failure mode. The rest is as stated.

verdicts.title: Candidate: Qwen3.6-27B
verdicts.reason: HF card: Apache-2.0, April 2026 citation, 27B, 64-layer hybrid layout, CC-OCR 81.2, OCRBench 89.4. The Qwen3.8 card lists OmniDocBench 1.5 at 89.4. The MWS and OCRBench v2 values match. The VRAM figure is inferred from Unsloth's 24 GB at 6-bit. The mmproj note is third-party, not Unsloth.

verdicts.reason: HF card: Apache-2.0, April 2026, OmniDocBench1.5 89.9, CC-OCR 81.9. OCRBench 90.0 comes from the Qwen3.6-27B card. MWS, OCRBench v2 (65.5/60.8) and the Unsloth memory and throughput figures match. vllm>=0.25.0 for NVFP4 is confirmed.

verdicts.reason: The card values (87.7/79.3/89.2), the Feb 2026 citation, Apache-2.0, MWS, OCRBench v2 58.7/64.1, the CC-OCR multilingual RU F1 78.97 (arxiv 2609.24058 Table 3) and Nanonets OmniDocBench 76.7 are confirmed. The listed 'MDPBench RU 60.3' is the JP column; RU is 54.7. Nanonets olmOCR 77.2 and IDP 76.2 were not visible in the fetched summaries.

verdicts.title: Candidate: PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 / 1.6
verdicts.reason: 'MDPBench RU 86.0, the highest in the table' is false: 86.0 is the KO column, RU is 76.0, and Gemini-3-pro scores 84.9. Real5 and OmniDocBench v1.6 values, the 0.9B size, Cyrillic edit distance 0.109, olmOCR 80.0 and GlotOCR Cyrillic Acc@5 78.0 (arxiv 2604.12978) are confirmed. The license is not stated in the paper.

verdicts.title: Candidate: Chandra OCR 2
verdicts.reason: github.com/datalab-to/chandra: ru 85.5% (Chandra 2) vs 88.7% (Chandra 1), 82.8% (Gemini 2.5 Flash) and 72.2% (GPT-5 Mini); olmOCR-bench 85.8 ± 0.8; 43-language average 77.8%; code Apache 2.0, weights modified OpenRAIL-M with a $2M cap and no use competing with Datalab's API; served via vLLM or HF. The repo does not state the parameter count (4B is unverified). Chandra 1 scores higher on Russian and was not considered.

verdicts.title: Candidate: Gemma 4 31B IT
verdicts.reason: The numbers match: OmniDocBench1.5 80.1 and CC-OCR 75.7 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B card), OCRBench 86.1 (Qwen3.6-27B card), MWS test KIE 0.793 and img→text 0.734. But the candidate URL points to a Qwen model card, not to a Gemma source. License, release date, serving and VRAM were not checked, so the entry has no primary source.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Benchmarks are confirmed only as third-party figures in Qwen cards and MWS. A Google model card URL is needed before the license or serving can be stated.

missing: MWS lists GLM-5.3 Flash with test grounding 0.613 (KIE 0.784), far above any Qwen. If it is open-weight and fits 32 GB, it matters for zoom_regions/zoom_source crop placement. The report never checked which non-Qwen MWS entries (GLM-5.3 Flash, Cotype Light 3, Cotype VL 32B 8-bit, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) are open-weight and runnable locally.

The benchmark's own split noise is as large as the model gaps: Qwen3.6-27B KIE is 0.833 on validation vs 0.893 on test, while Qwen3.8-27B is 0.812 vs 0.807. The validation-split KIE gap between the two Qwens is only 2 points, so the 8.6-point test gap should not be treated as reliable.

Video-5 evidence (README.md:36-43) contradicts 'segmentation is the main loss' for that video: 14/15 intervals detected, yet 6-7/22 fields wrong, partly from label-boundary ambiguity under the pre-11.10 address rule. The report needed a per-video error-class breakdown, not only the 4-video aggregate.

The official Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 checkpoint and the card's recommendation of vLLM/SGLang/TokenSpeed were not considered. A vLLM server on the RTX 5090 with continuous batching (leaf concurrency) could beat llama.cpp --parallel 1 on throughput without any model change.

Output-token and prompt-size levers on the current model: about 236 output tokens per call at 61 tok/s, with a ~24k-char instructions-plus-schema prompt. Image token limits (--image-max-tokens 4096) vs accuracy were not considered either.

The Unsloth throughput figures (160/240 tok/s, 140/220) are with MTP and partly at the UD-Q2_K_XL quant, so they cannot be compared directly with the deployed 61 tok/s at Q6 without MTP. The report treats them as a model-to-model decode ratio.
The MDPBench KO/RU column misread was carried into three places (findings 4 and 5, the Qwen3.5-9B and PaddleOCR candidates). Any downstream summary that quotes RU 86.0/85.5/61.9/60.3 is wrong.

verdicts.title: A/B Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.6-27B against the current Qwen3.8-27B on Russian field reading
verdicts.reason: I downloaded the MWS README (raw.githubusercontent.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench/main/README.md). Every quoted validation and test row matches exactly: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B val 0.694/0.859/0.784/0.099/0.822/0.904; Qwen3.6-27B test KIE 0.893; Qwen3.8-27B val 0.800 img->text, 0.812 KIE, 0.236 grounding. Habr 953292 confirms KIE is an F1 over fully matching key-value pairs and does not publish inference settings. The Qwen3.6-27B HF card confirms CC-OCR 81.2/81.9, OCRBench 89.4/90.0 and Apache-2.0. Unsloth card confirms UD-Q6_K 30 GB, UD-Q5_K_M 27.1 GB, UD-Q4_K_XL 22.9 GB. deploy/README.md:260 keeps 35B-A3B 'для исторического сравнения'.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The numbers are correct, but the claim needs four caveats. (1) The README has a seventh Anti-fraud column, which the report drops. Qwen3.8-27B is better there too (0.391 vs 0.232/0.195), though that is irrelevant here. (2) On the 119-item KIE subset, Qwen3.6-27B moves from 0.833 on val to 0.893 on test, which suggests KIE differences of 0.01-0.02 are noise. (3) deploy/ab_speed_test.sh compares two git refs against ONE shared model server and states it 'never changes ... the model service'. It runs one VIDEO per invocation and has no MODEL_PATH/MMPROJ_PATH inputs. A model A/B therefore means restarting sever-model with a different /etc/sever-tsl/local-model.env and running the same ref twice. That is not 'ab_speed_test.sh with only MODEL_PATH... swapped'. (4) The unsloth MTP repo cited for file sizes says '--mmproj [is] not yet supported with MTP', so a vision deployment must use the non-MTP GGUF, whose sizes may differ.

verdicts.title: Check that the local llama-server Q6 stack is not losing Russian OCR quality (MWS subset plus golden crops)
verdicts.reason: github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/22785: opened 7 May 2026, labelled bug-unconfirmed and stale, closed as not planned on 21 Jun 2026. It reports server-only OCR degradation since b8545 (last good b8533), projector qwen3vl_merger. ngxson replied 'The commit mentioned in "First Bad Commit" is unrelated'. The MindStudio article (30 Aug 2026) contains the BF16-projector and small-text quotes verbatim. The HF dataset card gives validation counts of 144 full-page OCR and 119 KIE.
